headline: TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, said it is in talks to join Elon Musk's planned Terafab chip complex in Texas, as long as TSMC runs the factory.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the CEO confirmed the talks on a record earnings call; the deal itself is not agreed.
importance_line: If a deal happens it could add US chip capacity for AI customers and Musk's companies, but TSMC and Musk have publicly differed on who would run the plant and nothing is signed.
summary: Fortune reports that C.C. Wei, chairman and CEO of Taiwan's TSMC, told analysts on its earnings call that the company is in discussions to be part of Terafab, the Texas chip complex planned by Tesla chief executive Elon Musk, but that any plant it joins "must be run by TSMC". Musk said earlier this month on X that his companies will build and run the fab and that TSMC would at most sublease part of it; TSMC also posted record quarterly net profit of about $24 billion, up 69%, and said demand for its chips is far above what it can supply.
notes: TSMC and Musk have differing public positions on control; plan still 'under deliberation' per Wei.
